claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys have a significant positive heat of mixing with Cu.
DFT simulations can predict the thermodynamic stability of RHEA–Cu composite structures.
DFT simulations can be used to optimize the alloy composition.
Optimizing composition through DFT can facilitate stable RHEA–Cu composite formation.
An optimized alloy composition can minimize the positive heat of mixing between refractory alloying elements and Cu.
Minimizing the positive heat of mixing facilitates large-scale reaction between RHEAs and Cu.
Minimizing the positive heat of mixing facilitates stable microstructure formation.
The optimized composition will reduce RHEA–Cu interfacial energy by 20%.
The interfacial energy will decrease from 0.5 J/m^2 to 0.4 J/m^2.
The unoptimized alloy composition has an interfacial energy of 0.5 J/m^2.
The proposed operating temperature range is 500–1000 K.
A temperature range of 500–1000 K is relevant to next-generation nuclear-reactor operation.
The proposed pressure range is 1–10 atm.
A pressure range of 1–10 atm is typical of reactor cooling systems.
Alloy-system complexity and limited experimental validation data may reduce the accuracy of the DFT predictions.
Optimized and unoptimized compositions will be compared, with the unoptimized composition serving as the control.
The hypothesis is falsified if the optimized composite is not at least 15% more stable than the unoptimized composite.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is defined as a 20% decrease in interfacial energy, whereas falsification is based on a 15% increase in an undefined measure of composite stability. These are not established as equivalent metrics, so the test does not directly evaluate the stated quantitative outcome.
